name: Bisdisulizole disodium
lead: Bisdisulizole disodium (trade name Neo Heliopan AP, from Symrise; also abbreviated DPDT) is a water-soluble organic UVA filter used in sunscreens [1]. It is a disodium salt with two sulfonated benzimidazole units on a phenylene core [1].
It has been approved in the European Union since 2000 at up to 10% in sunscreen formulations and is not approved in the United States [1].

paras: It absorbs UVA radiation and is used in sunscreen products, notably in water-based phases of formulations [1].
EU approval began in 2000 with a 10% limit; the US has not approved it [1]. The USAN Council adopted the nonproprietary name in April 2006 [1].

card.summary: Water-soluble UVA sunscreen filter (Neo Heliopan AP), EU-approved since 2000 and not approved in the US.

quick.overview:
Bisdisulizole disodium is a water-soluble UVA filter sold by Symrise as Neo Heliopan AP.

It is approved in the EU at up to 10% but not in the US. Few sources document it in detail.
quick.mechanism: It absorbs UVA radiation in the sunscreen formulation.
quick.risks: No safety information was found in the sources reviewed; it is not approved in the United States.
